title: UDLF deployment config — Splunk via contentctl v5.6
description: Config for `platform: splunk-contentctl-v5-6`. Emits a contentctl v5.6-shaped detection for the build pipeline. `type` is the discriminator. Closed, no `advanced`.

then.$comment: contentctl rejects an rba block on Hunting and Correlation detections: their default ESCU deployments do not enable risk-based alerting, so any risk config would be silently dropped or raise. The inverse rule — rba is *required* for TTP and Anomaly — is gated on the detection being production, which lives outside this block (UDLF `lifecycle: live`), so it is a deployer-side check rather than a schema constraint.
Hunting detections are never enabled on install.

schema.description: Sub-schema revision this block was authored against, e.g. `splunk-contentctl-v5-6::0.1.0`.

type.description: contentctl analytic type, the discriminator for this block. Selects the ESCU default deployment (and its schedule) and decides whether notables and RBA are emitted.

data_source.description: contentctl data sources this detection relies on. Each must resolve under the pack's `data_sources/`. Join several with ` AND `.

rba.description: Risk-Based Alerting. TTP and Anomaly only; contentctl rejects it on Hunting and Correlation.

message.description: Risk and notable message template. Every `$field$` token must be a field the search produces.
examples: A download cradle was executed on $dest$ by $user$

risk_objects.description: Entities that accrue risk. Score is per object, not per detection.

field.description: Search field holding the risk object. Must be present in the search.

score.description: Risk contributed each time the detection fires. contentctl caps this at 100, unlike raw Splunk ES.

threat_objects.description: Indicators associated with the risk event. May be empty, but contentctl requires the key to be present.

field.description: Search field holding the threat object. Must be present in the search.

type.description: Category of the threat object. contentctl's own spellings, enforced at build time with no `other` fallback. Differs from the Splunk RBA list; do not rewrite between them.

drilldown_searches.description: Drilldown searches surfaced with the alert. Omit to let contentctl generate defaults from the risk objects.

search.description: Drilldown SPL. May contain `%original_detection_search%`, substituted at build time.

earliest_offset.description: Start of the drilldown window. Required by contentctl, with no default. Commonly `$info_min_time$`.

latest_offset.description: End of the drilldown window. Required by contentctl, with no default. Commonly `$info_max_time$`.

enabled_by_default.description: Whether the saved search is enabled on install. Where the UDLF deployment `enabled` flag lands. contentctl permits `true` only for production TTP, Anomaly and Correlation.

explanation.description: Longer-form text for the ES Use Case Library. Omit to fall back to `detection_context.description`.

tags.description: contentctl's tags block. Only tags UDLF does not already own appear here.

asset_type.description: Type of asset the detection targets. contentctl enforces this closed list.

security_domain.description: ES security domain the detection belongs to.

product.description: Splunk products the detection is valid for.

group.description: Arbitrary grouping labels used by the content pack.

atomic_guid.description: Atomic Red Team test GUIDs this detection covers. Each must match an `auto_generated_guid`.

throttling.description: Alert suppression. Narrower period syntax than raw Splunk: seconds, minutes and hours only.

fields.description: Fields to suppress on. Each must appear in the search, and none may contain a space.

period.description: Suppression window in seconds, minutes or hours. No days: write one day as `86400s`, `1440m` or `24h`.

manual_test.description: Reason this detection cannot be tested automatically. Setting it makes contentctl skip its tests.

event_schema.description: Event schema the search is written against.

mappings.description: Custom field mappings. Loosely typed by contentctl and passed through unvalidated.

deployment.description: Inline deployment override. Normally omitted, since `type` resolves to a built-in ESCU deployment. Forces an Embedded deployment for this detection alone.

scheduling.description: Schedule override. contentctl requires all four keys when the block is present.

cron_schedule.description: Cron expression for the saved search.

earliest_time.description: Start of the search window as a Splunk relative-time modifier.

latest_time.description: End of the search window as a Splunk relative-time modifier.

schedule_window.description: How far the scheduler may delay the search.

alert_action.description: Alert action override. Only `notable` and `rba` are implemented; contentctl's email, slack and phantom models raise at serialize time.

notable.description: Notable event settings. contentctl requires all three keys when the block is present.

rule_title.description: Notable title. The built-in deployments use the literal `%name%`, substituted at build time.

rule_description.description: Notable description. The built-in deployments use the literal `%description%`.

nes_fields.description: Notable Event Suppression fields offered to the analyst.

rba.description: Whether risk-based alerting is emitted. On/off only; the risk objects live in the top-level `rba` block.

enabled.description: Turn RBA on for this detection. contentctl emits risk output only when true.
